value: For a select whose two arms are `<the value already in a register>` and `<a small constant>`, MWCC coalesces the arm that reuses the existing register into NOTHING and emits the layout `<branch-if-cond-true> ->TRUE_ARM ; <empty false arm> ; b ->END ; TRUE_ARM: <li>` - one branch MORE than the collapsed form. Which arm ends up empty follows the SOURCE order of the ternary operands, not the semantics, so `c ? 0 : v` and `!c ? v : 0` are NOT interchangeable at the object level: the first emits `bge ->END ; li rD,0` (2 insns) and the second emits `blt ->TRUE ; b ->END ; TRUE: li rD,0` (3 insns). When a target shows the three-instruction form and ours shows the two-instruction one, invert the ternary rather than probing register or schedule levers. Measured on game/enemy/critter::CritterGolemAI: rewriting `c->curmove < 0 ? 0 : c->curmove` as `c->curmove >= 0 ? c->curmove : 0` made 0xf0-0x104 byte-identical, took the opcode-multiset delta from 4 tokens to 1 and the regnorm genuine structural row count from 1 to 0, and raised fresh objdiff fuzzy 98.5874 -> 98.9963.
